## Reference repo for comparison

**Compare against:** https://github.com/Leantime/leantime (canonical upstream; MIT/AGPL, PHP/Laravel).

A planning agent doing a real comparison should pull the actual source, not just marketing pages. Suggested entry points in that repo:
- `README.md` — feature list + philosophy ("goals-focused PM for non-project managers; built with ADHD, autism, dyslexia in mind").
- `app/Domain/Goalcanvas/` and `app/Domain/Goals/` — the goals/goal-board model (Rhythm's biggest gap).
- `app/Domain/Tickets/` — Leantime's task ("ticket") model: statuses, tags, priority, milestones, dependencies, effort — compare field-by-field against Rhythm's `apps/api_server/src/models/task.ts`.
- `app/Domain/Timesheets/`, `app/Domain/Wiki/`, `app/Domain/Canvas/` — the strategy/collaboration layers we're deliberately **not** copying (see Out of scope).
- Views: Leantime renders Kanban / Table / List / Gantt / Calendar over the same tickets — the "one entity, many views" pattern this issue recommends adopting.

Rhythm side of the comparison lives in: `apps/api_server/src/models/{task,recurring_task_rule,project_template,project_instance,dashboard_summary,task_filter}.ts` and `apps/desktop_flutter/lib/features/tasks/`.

Decision record for this exploration: `docs/ai/decisions/2026-07-11-adopt-leantime-concepts-for-flexible-task-management-1037.md`.

---

## Summary

Exploration issue comparing [Leantime](https://github.com/Leantime/leantime) (open-source, goals-focused, neurodivergent-first project management) against Rhythm's current task management, to identify concepts/features/architecture that would make Rhythm **more flexible and usable** without diluting its differentiators (recurring **rhythms**, template-driven **projects**, and the **AI-agent** layer).

This is a research/planning issue — no implementation is committed yet. Each item below is a candidate for its own spec + PR.

## Context: what each product is

- **Leantime** — "goals-focused project management for non-project managers, built with ADHD, autism, and dyslexia in mind." Core thesis: keep people connected to *why* a task matters (goal → milestone → task) and make finishing feel good (progress donuts, emoji motivation rating). "As simple as Trello but as feature-rich as Jira," with many *views* over the same work.
- **Rhythm** — focused church-staff app whose differentiators Leantime lacks: **recurring rhythms** (weekly/monthly/annual, multi-step, sequential gating, per-step assignees), **template-driven projects** (offset-based steps anchored to a date), and **AI-agent integration** (Claude/Codex sessions, triggers, `preferredAgent` on tasks).

## Gap analysis

Rhythm's `Task` (`apps/api_server/src/models/task.ts`) currently has: title, notes, due/scheduled date, `scheduledOrder`, `locked`, a 4-value status (`open → in_progress → waiting_for_reply → done`), source provenance, calendar fields, owner, sharing, collaborators, `preferredAgent`. Confirmed **absent** from all data models: priority, tags/labels, subtasks, dependencies, effort estimates, goals, milestones.

| Concept | Leantime | Rhythm today | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Goals / OKRs** | Headline — goal boards, tasks roll up to goals | ✗ none | Biggest conceptual gap; most aligned with "flexibility" |
| **Kanban board view** | Yes | ✗ (list + weekly planner only) | High value, low risk |
| **Timeline / Gantt via milestones** | Yes | ✗ (projects are flat step lists) | Medium value |
| **Subtasks / dependencies** | Unlimited | ✗ (only `sequential` gating on rhythms) | Medium |
| **Tags / labels** | Yes | ✗ | Low-effort, high everyday utility |
| **Priority** | Yes | ✗ (only `scheduledOrder`) | Low-effort |
| **Dopamine design** (progress donuts, emoji motivation) | Signature | Partial — rhythms have `completionRatio`, no motivation signal | Cheap, on-brand |
| **Retrospectives / idea boards** | Yes | ✗ | Situational |
| **Time tracking, wiki, Lean/SWOT canvases** | Yes | ✗ | Skip — mismatched to church-staff audience |

## Proposed plan (ranked)

### 1. Goals as a first-class concept — *highest leverage*
Leantime's core insight, and it maps naturally onto Rhythm.
- New `goals` table; nullable `goalId` on `Task`, `ProjectInstance`, `RecurringTaskRule`.
- Dashboard already aggregates tasks/rhythms/projects (`dashboard_summary.ts`) — add a "progress toward goal" rollup + donut.
- For church staff a goal reads as a *season objective* ("Launch fall small-groups," "Easter services").
- **Additive migration, no breaking changes.** This is the change that most increases flexibility because it gives every other object a reason to exist.

### 2. Kanban board view over existing statuses — *cheapest win*
- The 4 statuses and `scheduledOrder` already exist → a board is almost pure UI.
- Drag-between-columns = a status PATCH already supported.
- New view in `features/tasks/views/`; **no API change.** Complements (does not replace) the weekly planner.

### 3. Tags + priority on tasks
- Two additive columns (`priority int`; `tags` via join table or JSON).
- Turns the existing `TaskFilter` (already built for status/date/search) into real cross-cutting organization ("show everything tagged #worship regardless of project").

### 4. Dopamine loop, lightly
- Surface the existing rhythm `completionRatio` as a **progress donut** + a small completion affirmation.
- Optional emoji "motivation/energy" tag on a task (one column) → a natural input for weekly-planner ordering; helps neurodivergent and busy users alike.

### 5. Milestones as optional grouping on projects — *only after #1*
- Leantime milestones group tasks with a date on a timeline. Rhythm projects are flat offset-step lists.
- Add optional milestone grouping + simple timeline view for larger multi-phase efforts (building project, capital campaign). Medium effort.

### Explicitly out of scope
Time tracking/timesheets, wikis, Lean/SWOT/Business-Model canvases, retrospectives — these serve Leantime's startup/agency audience, add surface area against Rhythm's simplicity, and don't fit church staff.

## Architecture note
Leantime's extensibility story is a PHP plugin marketplace + JSON-RPC API. **Don't chase that** — Rhythm's dual-endpoint + AI-agent architecture (`preferredAgent`, local agent server on :4001) is the more modern bet and its real differentiator. The one habit worth copying is Leantime's **"one entity, many views"** discipline: goals/board/timeline are all lenses over the same task rows. Rhythm's layered pattern (model → repo → controller → view) already supports adding views without touching data.

## Next steps
- [ ] Planning agent: clone https://github.com/Leantime/leantime and do a field-by-field comparison of its ticket/goal models against Rhythm's (paths above)
- [ ] Decide scope for first implementation PR (recommended: **Goals** or **Kanban view**)
- [ ] Spec the chosen item (schema/migration, API, Flutter view)
- [ ] Prototype on a feature branch and open a PR for local testing
